findings.current: Hyuk Mujin crumpled smoothly to the floor with a peaceful expression, and Cheongpung caught him.
findings.defect: The draft adds that Hyuk Mujin reaches the floor even though Cheongpung catches him as he collapses.
findings.rationale: The source says Cheongpung catches the collapsing Hyuk Mujin; it does not say that Hyuk Mujin falls to the floor.
findings.replacement: Hyuk Mujin crumpled with a peaceful expression, and Cheongpung caught him.
findings.source: 편안한 표정으로 스르륵 무너지는 혁무진을 청풍이 받아 들었다.

findings.current: “I want to stand on equal footing with him.”
findings.defect: Internal narration has been turned into dialogue that Taekyung audibly speaks.
findings.rationale: The source continues Taekyung’s unspoken explanation of his competitive pride; there are no quotation marks or speech attribution.
findings.replacement: I wanted to stand on equal footing with him.

findings.current: Grandson and disciple of the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
findings.defect: The draft replaces the source’s title “Sword God” with the distinct established title “Sword Saint.”
findings.rationale: This occurrence explicitly says 검신, whereas the source later uses 검성 when calling Mae Jonghak the Sword Saint; the distinction must be preserved.
findings.replacement: Grandson and disciple of the Sword God Mae Jonghak.

findings.current: He remembered that crude blue-steel sword and those footsteps.
findings.defect: The draft applies the crudeness only to the sword and renders martial footwork as generic footsteps.
findings.rationale: The coordinated phrase characterizes both Cheongpung’s sword and his 발걸음 as unrefined; in this duel context, 발걸음 denotes his footwork.
findings.replacement: He remembered Cheongpung’s crude blue-steel sword and clumsy footwork.

findings.current: Heaven’s Gate Temple was certainly the greatest educational institution in the orthodox Murim, but not every genius under heaven became a disciple of Heaven’s Gate Temple.
findings.defect: The institutional status 관도 is rendered as “disciple,” obscuring the contrast with the lineage disciples mentioned immediately afterward.
findings.rationale: 관도 means a student or cadet of the educational institution, while the next sentence separately refers to 적전 제자, direct lineage disciples.
findings.replacement: Heaven’s Gate Temple was certainly the greatest educational institution in the orthodox Murim, but not every genius under heaven became a student at Heaven’s Gate Temple.
findings.source: 천무학관(天武學館)은 분명 정파 무림 최고의 교육 기관이지만 천하의 모든 기재가 천무학관의 관도가 되는 것은 아니다.

findings.defect: The System attribute 근맥 is reduced to “Meridians,” omitting its sinew or muscular component and changing the affected stat.
findings.rationale: 근맥 denotes the body’s sinews or muscles together with its meridians; it is not synonymous with meridians alone.

findings.current: But why did you suddenly try to open the Conception and Governor Vessels? You’re not a Peak internal-energy master, and you’re not reckless enough to risk something like that.
findings.defect: Calling Taekyung insufficiently reckless reverses Hyuk Mujin’s jab that he lacks the nerve to take such a risk.
findings.rationale: 간 큰 means bold or gutsy; Hyuk Mujin is teasing Taekyung for lacking courage, not crediting him with prudent restraint.
findings.replacement: But why did you suddenly try to open the Conception and Governor Vessels? You’re not a Peak internal-energy master, and you don’t have the guts to risk something like that.
findings.source: 그런데 갑자기 임독양맥은 왜 건드리신 겁니까? 조장님이 절정 내가고수도 아니고, 그렇다고 위험을 감수할 만큼 간 큰 분도 아니시잖아요.

summary: Two critical changes introduce an unperformed fall and convert internal narration into spoken dialogue. Additional findings concern a changed title, omitted martial footwork characterization, institutional hierarchy, a mistranslated System attribute, and a softened jab.
